title: What Is a Good MYP Extended Mathematics Grade?
summary: Learn what counts as a good MYP Extended Mathematics grade, how internal criteria and eAssessment boundaries work, with a clear grading example.
body_markdown:
A **good MYP Extended Mathematics grade** is generally a **5 or 6 out of 7** . A 5 shows generally high-quality achievement, while a 6 indicates extensive understanding and increasingly independent mathematical thinking. A 7 is exceptional, but it is not the only result that demonstrates strong preparation for further mathematics.


Interpreting the grade requires an important distinction. Classroom assessment normally combines four criterion levels into a total out of 32, whereas the **MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment** converts examination marks using session-specific boundaries. Both systems produce grades from 1 to 7, but their conversion processes are different.


### What counts as a good MYP Extended Mathematics grade?


The practical meaning of a result depends on the student's goals, previous attainment, and intended next course.


Final grade Practical interpretation


**7** Exceptional understanding, reasoning, and transfer to unfamiliar problems


**6** Very strong performance with extensive understanding and frequent independence


**5** A good, secure result showing generally high-quality work


**4** Sound achievement, although demanding problems may still require support


**3** Acceptable achievement with noticeable gaps or inconsistency


**1--2** Limited achievement requiring substantial consolidation


Official MYP descriptors characterize grade 4 work as **good-quality work** , so a 4 is not automatically a failure. However, **5 or above** is usually a stronger benchmark because it indicates more secure understanding across familiar and unfamiliar situations.


For students considering a demanding Diploma Programme mathematics course, a consistent **6 or 7** is encouraging. It is not an official admission requirement. Schools establish their own placement policies and may also consider algebraic fluency, assessment history, work habits, and teacher recommendations.


### Extended Mathematics and Standard Mathematics


The IB allows MYP mathematics to be taught at two levels of challenge. Standard Mathematics develops a sound knowledge of basic principles, while **Extended Mathematics adds topics and skills for greater breadth and depth** .


A 5 in Extended Mathematics represents achievement against Extended Mathematics demands, not a lower version of a Standard Mathematics grade. There is no official conversion formula between the two courses.


The[IB MYP final statistical bulletin for May 2025](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/about-the-ib/pdfs/myp-final-statistical-bulletin-may-2025_en.pdf) reported a mean Extended Mathematics grade of **4.7** among 2,571 candidates. Approximately **54.5%** received grades 5--7, including **13.1%** who earned a 7. These figures provide context, but grades are not allocated by ranking candidates against fixed percentages.


### How internal MYP Extended Mathematics grading works


Classroom MYP Mathematics assessment uses four equally weighted criteria, each awarded a final achievement level from **0 to 8** .


Criterion What it assesses


**A: Knowing and understanding** Selecting and applying mathematical knowledge


**B: Investigating patterns** Developing general rules and justifying conclusions


**C: Communicating** Presenting notation, reasoning, and representations clearly


**D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts** Modelling, interpreting, and evaluating results


Teachers use professional judgment and the available evidence to identify the level that best represents demonstrated achievement. They do not normally calculate each criterion level by mechanically averaging every task mark.


The four final levels are added to produce a maximum of 32:


Criterion total=A+B+C+D\\text{Criterion total}=A+B+C+D


Criterion total


=


A


+


B


+

D


Criterion total Final grade


**28--32** **7**


**24--27** **6**


**19--23** **5**


**15--18** **4**


**10--14** **3**


**6--9** **2**


**1--5** **1**


**0** No grade awarded


These are criterion-total boundaries for school-based assessment, not percentage boundaries for the external examination.


### Worked internal-grading example


Suppose a student receives final levels of **A: 7, B: 6, C: 6, and D: 5** . The total is:


7+6+6+5=247+6+6+5=24

A total of **24 out of 32** converts to a **grade 6** . Although 24/32 equals 75%, this does not mean 75% on every MYP test earns a 6. The grade results from criterion judgments and the total boundary rather than a universal percentage scale.


Criterion D is the weakest area in this example. The student should therefore prioritize modelling, assumptions, units, interpretation, and evaluation instead of completing only routine calculations.


### How the MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment is graded


Students seeking an official MYP course result in Extended Mathematics complete an externally marked **on-screen examination** . The official[MYP Mathematics subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-mathematics-en.pdf) identifies three broad tasks:


Examination task Criteria emphasized


Knowing and understanding A and C


Investigating patterns B and C


Applying mathematics in real-life contexts C and D


Each task normally contains **31--35 marks** , subject to small blueprint variations. Criterion C appears throughout the examination, so clear methods, notation, representations, and explanations matter across all tasks.


IB-appointed examiners award raw marks using examination mark schemes. The IB then establishes subject- and session-specific boundaries through grade awarding, considering expert judgment of candidate work alongside statistical evidence. Boundaries may change when one examination is slightly more or less demanding than another.


Students must not apply the internal **24/32 = grade 6** boundary to an eAssessment mark. The IB's[assessment principles document](https://ibo.org/contentassets/1cdf850e366447e99b5a862aab622883/assessment-principles-and-practices-2018-en.pdf) explains why raw marks and grades are distinct.


### Does a grade 3 mean the student passed?


The IB does not assign a universal passing score to an individual MYP course. Schools decide how subject results affect internal progression and course placement.


For the full MYP certificate, the[IB grading and awards requirements](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/grading-and-awards/) require at least **grade 3 in every required eAssessment component** , at least **28 points out of 56** overall, completion of the required components, and fulfilment of the school's service as action expectations. A 3 can satisfy the component minimum, but it remains an acceptable rather than strong Extended Mathematics result.


### How to improve from a 4 or 5 to a 6


Students should diagnose performance by criterion rather than simply repeating familiar exercises.


- **Criterion A:** Correct conceptual gaps, then apply methods in unfamiliar combinations.
- **Criterion B:** Form conjectures, develop general rules, test them, and justify why they work.
- **Criterion C:** Show ordered working, define variables, label graphs, and use precise notation.
- **Criterion D:** Build appropriate models, interpret answers, examine assumptions, and evaluate reasonableness.


After each timed task, classify lost marks as conceptual errors, poor method selection, inaccurate execution, weak justification, unclear communication, or time-management problems. This creates a more useful revision plan than recording only a percentage.


Students can use[RevisionDojo MYP Extended Mathematics lessons](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics/learn) to rebuild weak concepts and the[Extended Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics/questionbank) for targeted practice. The guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) can help students translate knowledge into criterion-specific evidence.


### Common mistakes when interpreting grades


A raw test mark, criterion level out of 8, total out of 32, and final grade out of 7 represent different assessment stages. Treating them all as percentages leads to inaccurate predictions.


Internal grades also cannot guarantee eAssessment results because the external examination is independently marked and uses session-specific boundaries. Finally, calculation alone is insufficient: investigation, communication, modelling, interpretation, and evaluation all contribute to achievement.


### Conclusion


A good MYP Extended Mathematics grade is usually **5 or 6** , while a 7 represents exceptional achievement. Internally, four criterion levels produce a total out of 32; externally, examination marks are converted using boundaries established for that session.


Students aiming to improve should respond to criterion-specific feedback rather than chase an assumed percentage. RevisionDojo's Extended Mathematics Study Notes, Questionbank, and Jojo AI explanations can support focused practice where particular concepts or assessment skills remain weak.
